correctness.rationale: An entry at (i,j) appears in every corner from i to j; weight below three is therefore confined to the diagonal and first superdiagonal. The allowable nonzero supports are at most two diagonal positions, or a nonzero first-superdiagonal entry and its two adjacent diagonal positions, where both nonzero corners have rank one. Avoiding these supports is exactly the pair and adjacent-triple independence condition on parity-check columns. The one-error syndromes exhaust the syndrome space once the diagonal directions exhaust projective space. At α=2 the adjacent pair already spans the syndrome space; α=1 would give n=1 and no nonzero weight-three codeword. For α≥3, one may choose each adjacent image outside the corresponding two-space, independently. A projective direction of the sum of two independent representatives supplies an explicit three-diagonal dependence, so the distance is exactly three over every finite field, not just primes. Higher coordinates cannot affect the low-weight test. The syndrome maps are surjective and changing the quotient basis acts freely, giving the stated count. Inspected VERIFICATION.md and the nested verification/verify.py and verification/verify_output.txt: the finite checks cover four prime-field parameters and not general prime powers or all kernels. Independently, the binary case gives 21+6·4=45 weight-two words and the code count 30·2^57. No uploaded code was run.

The complete diagonal directions follow by substituting the prior length formula into the pair test. So the coded parameters and the complete parity-check choices follow from these two results by dimension-independent linear algebra.
The same lists of independent choices give n!, (q−1)^n, (q^α−q²)^{n−1}, and q^{α(n−1)(n−2)/2}. The only quotient is the standard free GL(α,q) change of basis of U_n/ker H.
